Audio Priority Bar 2.10.0 shows a muted microphone in red in the menu bar, with an option to stop its pulse, and lifts a dragged row on the panel's own material. Coming from 2.9.2, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Menu bar

- A muted microphone now shows in red in the menu bar, while the other glyphs keep following a light or dark menu bar ([#49](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/49)).
- **Pulse muted microphone** in Settings › Menu Bar turns the pulse off for anyone who finds it distracting, without turning on Reduce Motion everywhere ([#49](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/49), [#50](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/50)).

## Panel

- A row you drag to rerank now lifts on a frosted material that matches the translucent panel, instead of a dark slab in dark mode ([#51](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/51)).

## Updates

- Updating from 2.9.0 or later downloads only what changed. Older versions download the full archive.

## Thanks

Thanks to @DigiH for the red muted microphone and the pulse setting ([#49](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/49)), and for reporting the dim microphone fixed in [#50](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/50).

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
